knowledge:
- key_parameters: eset=An ExpressionSet or a log2-normalized gene expression matrix (genes as rows, samples as columns) ;; labels=A character vector of group labels for each sample in eset (must be legal R variable names) ;; contrast=A character string specifying the comparison of interest (e.g., "treatment-mock") ;; geneSets=A vector (single gene set) or list of vectors (multiple gene sets) containing gene symbols matching the rownames of eset ;; pairVector=An optional vector of sample/patient IDs used to specify paired or longitudinal samples ;; fixed=A formula specifying the fixed effects for the qgen mixed model ;; contrast.factor=A formula specifying the factor of interest for the contrast in qgen ;; random=A formula specifying the random effects structure in qgen ;; correlation=An optional corStruct object specifying the correlation structure in qgen ;; design.sampleid=A character string indicating the column name in the metadata that matches the sample IDs in the expression data
- alternatives: LIMMA=Mentioned as an alternative for individual gene statistics, but qusage's implemented Welch-based method is preferred as it is shown to improve specificity ;; Wu et al. (2012)=Mentioned as the basis for the VIF technique, which qusage extends
- when_to_use: Use when performing gene set enrichment analysis on transcriptomics data (especially microarray, but adaptable to RNA-seq count data) and you want to account for inter-gene correlation, obtain full probability density functions of pathway activity, perform paired/longitudinal analysis, or run complex linear mixed models.
- pitfalls: Rownames of eset must match the gene symbols/IDs used in the geneSets list, otherwise gene sets will be evaluated as size 0 ;; Group labels must be legal R variable names (no spaces, must start with a letter) ;; For best results, the expression dataset should be trimmed to remove genes with very low expression ;; Multiple hypothesis testing correction (e.g., FDR) must be manually applied to the resulting p-values when analyzing a large number of gene sets.

workflows.name: standard_qusage_analysis
workflows.intent: Perform standard gene set enrichment analysis on a single dataset, calculate p-values, adjust for multiple testing, and visualize pathway activity.
input: eset (matrix or ExpressionSet of log2-normalized gene expression data)
gene_sets.gmt (GMT file containing gene sets of interest)
workflows.stages: 1. Read gene sets from a GMT file using read.gmt ;; 2. Run the qusage wrapper function to calculate gene-level comparisons, aggregate gene data, and calculate variance inflation factors ;; 3. Extract p-values using pdf.pVal ;; 4. Adjust p-values for multiple testing using p.adjust ;; 5. Generate a summary table of results using qsTable ;; 6. Plot confidence intervals or density curves using plot or plotDensityCurves
workflows.code:
MSIG.geneSets = read.gmt("c2.cp.kegg.v4.0.symbols.gmt")
qs.results.msig = qusage(eset, labels, contrast, MSIG.geneSets)
p.vals = pdf.pVal(qs.results.msig)
q.vals = p.adjust(p.vals, method="fdr")
qsTable(qs.results.msig, number=10)
plot(qs.results.msig)

workflows.name: two_way_comparison
workflows.intent: Compare pathway activation profiles between two distinct groups or conditions over a treatment/time course (differential pathway activation).
input: eset (matrix or ExpressionSet of log2-normalized gene expression data)
gene_sets.gmt (GMT file containing gene sets of interest)
workflows.stages: 1. Define group labels and sample pairing information ;; 2. Run qusage for each individual group comparison, or run a single qusage call with a complex contrast representing the difference of differences ;; 3. Calculate p-values for the difference between the two curves using twoCurve.pVal or pdf.pVal ;; 4. Visualize the comparative density curves, gene set distributions, and individual gene confidence intervals using plotDensityCurves, plotGeneSetDistributions, and plotCIsGenes
workflows.code:
pairs = c(1:17,1:17)
twoWay.labels = paste(resp, labels, sep=".")
sx.results  = qusage(eset, twoWay.labels, "sx.t1-sx.t0",
                     MSIG.geneSets, pairVector=pairs)
asx.results = qusage(eset, twoWay.labels, "asx.t1-asx.t0", 
                     MSIG.geneSets, pairVector=pairs)
p.vals = twoCurve.pVal(sx.results,asx.results)
asx.vs.sx = qusage(eset, twoWay.labels, "(sx.t1-sx.t0) - (asx.t1-asx.t0)",
                 MSIG.geneSets, pairVector=pairs)
p.vals = pdf.pVal(asx.vs.sx)
plotDensityCurves(asx.results,path.index=125,xlim=c(-0.2,0.5),
                  col=3,main="CYTOSOLIC DNA SENSING")
plotDensityCurves(sx.results,path.index=125,col=2,add=T)
plotDensityCurves(asx.vs.sx, path.index=125,col=1,add=T, lwd=3)
plotGeneSetDistributions(sx.results,asx.results,path.index=125)
plotCIsGenes(sx.results,path.index=125)

workflows.name: mixed_models_qgen
workflows.intent: Perform gene set enrichment analysis using generalized linear mixed models to account for random effects and complex correlation structures.
input: eset.full (matrix or ExpressionSet of log2-normalized gene expression data)
flu.meta (data frame containing sample metadata and design variables)
workflows.stages: 1. Define formulas for fixed effects and contrast factors ;; 2. Run the qgen function specifying fixed effects, random effects, and sample IDs ;; 3. Optionally define a correlation structure and run qgen with correlation constraints ;; 4. Summarize and plot the mixed model results
workflows.code:
fixedeffects <- ~Hours+Condition+Condition*Hours+Age+Gender
con.fac <- ~Condition*Hours
contrast = "sx77 - sx0"
qusage.result.random<-qgen(eset.full,flu.meta,
                           fixed=fixedeffects,
                           contrast.factor=con.fac, 
                           contrast=contrast,
                           geneSets=ISG.geneSet,
                           random=~1|Subject,
                           design.sampleid="SampleID")
qsTable(qusage.result.random)
corStruct = corExp(value=3,~Hours.Numeric|Subject)
qusage.result.corstruct<-qgen(eset.full,flu.meta,
                              fixed=fixedeffects,
                              contrast.factor=con.fac, 
                              contrast=contrast,
                              geneSets=ISG.geneSet,
                              correlation=corStruct,
                              design.sampleid="SampleID")

workflows.name: meta_analysis
workflows.intent: Combine pathway enrichment probability density functions (PDFs) from multiple independent studies to perform a meta-analysis.
input: fluVaccine (a list containing expression datasets and associated metadata for multiple studies)
BTM.geneSets (list of gene sets of interest)
workflows.stages: 1. Run qusage independently on each dataset to generate a list of QSarray objects ;; 2. Combine the individual study PDFs using combinePDFs ;; 3. Calculate meta-analysis p-values using pdf.pVal ;; 4. Plot the combined meta-analysis PDF alongside individual study PDFs using plotCombinedPDF
workflows.code:
qs.results.list = lapply(c("GSE59635", "GSE59654"), function(n){
  eset = fluVaccine$esets[[n]]
  phenoData = fluVaccine$phenoData[[n]]
  labels = paste(phenoData$responder, phenoData$bloodDrawDay, 
                 sep = ".")
  qusage(eset, labels, "(high.d7-high.d0)-(low.d7-low.d0)", 
            BTM.geneSets, pairVector=phenoData$subjectId, n.points=2^14)
})
combined = combinePDFs(qs.results.list)
head(pdf.pVal(combined))
plotCombinedPDF(combined, path.index=235)
